# Problem1
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)
library(patchwork)
data("ny_noaa")
```

```{r}
ny_noaa |>
  summarise(
    across(
      everything(),
      ~sum(is.na(.x))
    )
  )
ny_noaa|>
  summarise(
    across(
      everything(),
      ~mean(is.na(.x))*100
    )
  )
```

This dataset contains daily weather observations from weather stations across New York State from January 1, 1981, through December 31, 2010. It contains station identifiers(`id`), observation dates(`date`), precipitation(`prcp`), snowfall(`snow`), snow depth(`snwd`), maximum temperature(`tmax`), and minimum temperature(`tmin`). The dataset contains `r nrow(ny_noaa)` observations and `r ncol(ny_noaa)` variables.

Missingness varies across variables. The station ID and date have no missing values. Precipitation has relatively little missing data (5.62%), while snowfall and snow depth have 14.7% and 22.8% missing, respectively. Maximum and minimum temperatures have the highest missingness, at approximately 43.7% each.


```{r}
ny_noaa_clean = 
  ny_noaa|>
  separate(
    date,
    into = c("year","month","day"),
    sep = "-"
  )|>
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(year),
    month = as.integer(month),
    day = as.integer(day),
    prcp = as.numeric(prcp)/10,
    snow = as.numeric(snow)/10,
    snwd = as.numeric(snwd)/10,
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax)/10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin)/10
  )
```

I converted year, month, and day to integer, precipitation, snowfall, and snow depth to centimeters, and maximum and minimum temperature to degrees Celsius.


```{r}
ny_noaa_clean|>
  filter(!is.na(snow))|>
  count(snow, sort = T)|>
  slice_head(n=10)
```

The most common snowfall value is 0, because snowfall does not occur on most observation days.


```{r}
temp_by_station = 
  ny_noaa_clean|>
  filter(month ==1|month ==7)|>
  group_by(id, year, month)|>
  summarise(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = T),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(temp_by_station,
       aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax, group = id))+
  geom_line(alpha=0.3)+
  facet_grid(. ~ month)+
  labs(
    title = "Average Maximum Temperature in January and July",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average Maximum Temperature"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Average maximum temperatures are generally high in July than in January, reflecting seasonal differences. Temperatures vary across stations and years. A few potential outliers are observed, including January temperatures below -10°C and July temperatures as low as approximately 15°C, which are substantially lower than those at other stations.


```{r}
p1 = 
  ggplot(
    ny_noaa_clean,
    aes(x=tmin,y=tmax)
  )+
  geom_bin2d()+
  labs(
    title = "Maximum vs Minimum Temperature",
    x = "Minimum Temperature (°C)",
    y = "Maximum Temperature (°C)"
  )+
  theme_minimal()

snow_by_year = 
  ny_noaa_clean|>
  filter(snow>0, snow<100)
p2 = 
  ggplot(
    snow_by_year,
    aes(x=factor(year),y=snow)
  )+
  geom_boxplot()+
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of snowfall by year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Snowfall (cm)"
  )+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 90,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )

p1 + p2
```

Maximum and minimum temperatures show a positive relationship. Most observations are concentrated in the central region, while some extreme values are present. Some extreme values, such as temperatures of 60°C recorded at one station on multiple consecutive days, may indicate potential data quality issues.

snowfall distributions are generally similar across years, with relatively low medians. Many high outliers are present in each year, with some observations exceeding 50cm. Although the maximum snowfall values vary across years, there is no clear overall trend in the distributions over time.
